sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Long-running agents should not necessarily execute entirely inside a single synchronous HTTP request.

- Long-running agents should not necessarily execute entirely inside a single synchronous HTTP request.
- An unguessable task identifier is not sufficient access control.
- 27.3 Scalability mathematics If the average arrival rate is 20 tasks per second and average execution duration is 15 seconds: \[ L=\lambda W=20\times15=300 \] The application needs to support approximately 300 in-flight tasks on average under stable conditions.
- If each task makes six LLM calls averaging 3,000 billable tokens: \[ TokensPerMinute= 20\times60\times6\times3000 \] \[ =21.6\ million \] The provider's quota, burst capacity and infrastructure must support this demand.
- Autoscaling application containers alone will not solve a model-provider quota bottleneck.
- 27.4 Noisy-neighbor isolation Use per-tenant quotas, fair scheduling, independent ingestion and query capacity, concurrency limits and cost reservations.

sections.title: 27.1 Asynchronous task API
sections.body:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Frontend
    participant A as FastAPI
    participant Q as Queue
    participant W as Agent Worker
    participant D as State Database

    U->>A: POST /tasks
    A->>D: Create authorized task
    A->>Q: Enqueue execution
    A-->>U: 202 Accepted + task ID
    Q->>W: Deliver task
    W->>D: Persist progress
    U->>A: GET /tasks/{id}
    A->>D: Read authorized status
    A-->>U: Current task state
```

sections.title: 27.2 API endpoints
sections.body:
| Endpoint | Purpose |
|--------|--------|
| `POST /tasks` | Create an authorized agent task |
| `GET /tasks/{id}` | Retrieve permitted task status |
| `GET /tasks/{id}/events` | Stream sanitized progress |
| `POST /tasks/{id}/cancel` | Request cancellation |
| `POST /approvals/{id}/decision` | Submit authenticated approval |
| `GET /tasks/{id}/artifacts` | Retrieve authorized outputs |

Every task endpoint requires ownership or appropriate organizational authorization.

An unguessable task identifier is not sufficient access control.

sections.title: 27.4 Noisy-neighbor isolation
sections.body:
Use per-tenant quotas, fair scheduling, independent ingestion and query capacity, concurrency limits and cost reservations.

An agent that launches 100 concurrent subagents can exhaust shared resources even if its parent request count is only one.

Rate limits should account for execution work, not just HTTP request volume.

- Use per-tenant quotas, fair scheduling, independent ingestion and query capacity, concurrency limits and cost reservations.
- An agent that launches 100 concurrent subagents can exhaust shared resources even if its parent request count is only one.
- Rate limits should account for execution work, not just HTTP request volume.

steps.label: Load
steps.narration: Loading converts PDFs, DOCX, CSV, HTML and other sources into a consistent document object with text plus metadata.

steps.label: Clean
steps.narration: Cleaning removes boilerplate, normalizes unicode, strips headers/footers, and prepares text so chunking and embeddings stay high quality.

steps.label: Chunk
steps.narration: Chunking splits documents into retrieval units. Size and overlap control whether evidence is complete enough without adding noise.

steps.label: Embed
steps.narration: Embedding turns each chunk into a dense vector so semantically similar questions and passages can be matched.

steps.label: Index
steps.narration: Indexing stores vectors (and often sparse signals) for fast nearest-neighbor search with filters for tenant, source, or time.

steps.label: Retrieve
steps.narration: Retrieval finds the Top-K chunks for a query using dense, sparse, or hybrid search before generation.
